transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I keep getting stuck redoing the same checks and routines over and over at work, even when I know they’re unnecessary, and it’s starting to derail my projects and my life. It's reached a point where I just can't seem to break the cycle on my own.
Do you feel like you are repeating these routines to prevent a specific feared outcome or bad event from happening, or is it more of a need to perform the action until it feels 'just right'?

It is definitely to prevent a specific bad outcome; I get looping thoughts that if I miss a tiny detail like a wrong bolt size, a part will fail and people will get hurt. To prevent that, I end up opening the same CAD files or emails ten times in a row to recheck them. Even though I know the fear is irrational, I just can't seem to stop.
Do you also experience intrusive, unwanted thoughts or images about these accidents that pop into your head even when you are not actively working?

Yes, I do. I get these vivid, looping mental images of parts failing and people getting hurt because of a tiny detail I might have missed, like a minor tolerance error. Even when I'm away from work, I know it's irrational, but I find it incredibly difficult to shut those catastrophic thoughts out of my head.

When you are stuck in these cycles, do you find that you spend more time performing these repetitive checking behaviors, or are you primarily preoccupied with the intrusive mental thoughts themselves?

It is really a combination of both, but the physical checking is what consumes the vast majority of my actual time. The looping, intrusive thoughts of catastrophic failure trigger the anxiety, but then I'll spend an hour clicking back and forth, opening the same CAD file ten times in a row just to do "one more pass."
